Polish Utility Launches New Smart Meter Platform to Boost Grid Efficiency

WARSAW—Poland’s electric utilities sector welcomed a significant technological advancement on Monday as PolEnergia, a leading national energy provider, announced the launch of its new smart meter platform designed to support real-time monitoring and energy usage optimization for residential and business customers.

The new platform, named EnergoVista, was unveiled at a press conference held at PolEnergia’s Warsaw headquarters. Executives highlighted the platform’s advanced data analytics and remote management capabilities, which are expected to enhance grid reliability and empower consumers to better manage their electricity consumption.

“EnergoVista represents a major step forward in modernizing Poland’s electricity infrastructure,” said Michał Nowakowski, CEO of PolEnergia. “With this system, we can respond more rapidly to changes in demand, reduce operational costs, and help customers make informed decisions about their energy use.”

According to company officials, the first phase of the rollout will see approximately 400,000 smart meters installed across the Mazowieckie and Śląskie provinces by the end of 2024. The company aims to reach over 1.2 million households and businesses nationwide within three years.

Industry observers have welcomed the development. Ewa Zielińska, spokesperson for the Polish Association of Energy Consumers, commented, “Smart metering is a key element in building a more flexible and sustainable energy system. Consumers will benefit from greater transparency in billing and the ability to adjust their usage patterns according to real-time pricing signals.”

The platform also includes features to support integration with renewable energy sources, such as solar panels, which officials say aligns with Poland’s ongoing efforts to decarbonize its power sector. “The system’s compatibility with distributed generation will be especially important as more customers install solar and other clean technologies,” said Jakub Kowalczyk, an analyst at Energia21.

PolEnergia has confirmed that the rollout will be accompanied by a public information campaign, with support lines and online resources available to assist customers in adapting to the new technology.

The company’s initiative comes as Poland continues to invest in grid modernization, aiming to improve efficiency and meet EU energy targets in the coming decade.
